sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
A RAG deployment may change several components:

- Parsing configuration.
- Chunking algorithm.
- Embedding model.
- Vector index parameters.
- Retrieval strategy.
- Reranker.
- Prompt.
- Generation model.
- Authorization policy.

Each component should be independently versioned.

### Example release gates

| Metric | Current version | Candidate version | Decision |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Recall\@10 | 88% | 92% | Pass |
| Faithfulness | 91% | 94% | Pass |
| Table answer accuracy | 86% | 72% | Fail |
| Unauthorized retrieval tests | 0 failures | 0 failures | Pass |
| p95 latency | 2.1 s | 2.8 s | Pass if within SLO |
| Cost per request | \$0.003 | \$0.004 | Review |

Even though the candidate has better overall retrieval and faithfulness, the table-quality regression should prevent automatic promotion if financial-table accuracy is a mandatory requirement.

steps.label: Query
steps.narration: The user query enters the system and may need rewriting before search.

steps.label: Transform
steps.narration: Query transformation expands, rewrites, or decomposes the question to improve recall.

steps.label: Search
steps.narration: Dense and/or keyword search return candidate passages.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.narration: Fusion methods such as RRF combine rankings from multiple retrievers into one list.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.narration: A cross-encoder or LLM reranker reorders candidates for higher precision context.

steps.label: Context
steps.narration: Final context is budgeted, ordered, and injected into the prompt for grounded generation.
